system: You are Claude acting as Sarah's read-only engineering partner. Inspect the repository directly with Read/Glob/Grep. Be concise, evidence-based, and practical. Do not modify files or workflows. Do not inspect, alter, or advise changes to The Room or Emily/Olivia workflows or source. Focus only on experiments/little-world-lab and .github/workflows/little-world-falcon-live.yml.
prompt: Review the Cedar Hollow natural-action selection bias after the completed temperature sweep. Inspect experiments/little-world-lab/falcon_live.py, living_world.py, tests/test_falcon_live.py, and .github/workflows/little-world-falcon-live.yml. The same three seeds at temperatures 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 produced model-chosen counts 72 move/0 others; 72 move/0 others; and 69 move + 3 observe, with 0 backend errors. Feasible actions were much broader, including work/rest/observe on all 72 decisions and talk/help on most. Determine the single most diagnostic next experiment that does NOT force behavior and preserves WorldEngine authority. In particular, assess whether JSON-schema oneOf branch ordering is a plausible confound given the current _response_schema order, and whether a controlled schema-order permutation test is worth implementing before testing a larger model. If yes, specify the smallest exact code/workflow change and the minimum permutations needed. If no, explain the better next experiment. Do not recommend canned dialogue, action quotas, prompt rules that prescribe behavior, or weaker validation.
context: Run #12 completed successfully; 27 tests passed and all six directed action contracts still passed.
At temperature 0.1, chosen_action_counts were move=72 and all other actions=0.
At temperature 0.5, chosen_action_counts were move=72 and all other actions=0.
At temperature 1.0, chosen_action_counts were move=69, observe=3, and talk/help/work/rest=0.
Current FalconBackend._response_schema constructs oneOf branches in order rest, observe, then move if feasible, then talk, help, work.
Instrumentation distinguishes feasibility, model choice, engine rejection, and resolved action.
No Room or Emily/Olivia files are in scope.
expected_response: Start with VERDICT: schema-order-test / different-test. Then give: (1) why, grounded in exact code, (2) smallest experiment, (3) exact minimal patch shape, (4) what result would support schema/decoder bias versus Falcon-1B capability bias.
